title: Mission 12: The Sweep
story: Compliance week. Somewhere in the department's sprawling project tree are oversized files, forgotten configs, world-writable time bombs and empty husks - and the compliance officer wants each category on its own list by tonight. You cannot walk a tree this deep by hand. find walks it for you, testing every file against any condition you can name.

badge.name: The Sweep: Nothing Hides
badge.desc: Mastered find by sweeping a deep tree for names, sizes, types, permissions and emptiness.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING12.txt in your department directory. FROM the sweep/ directory, find every file named exactly 'settings.conf' anywhere under projects/ and save find's output (the paths, as it prints them) to conf_list.txt.

checks.fail: conf_list.txt must hold the paths of every settings.conf under projects/ (run find from sweep/ against the relative name projects).

tasks.brief: All the leftover editor droppings: every file matching *.swp under projects/, to swp_list.txt (same rules: run from sweep/, save find's paths).

checks.fail: swp_list.txt must list every *.swp file under projects/ (quote the pattern so the shell does not expand it).

tasks.brief: The org chart needs every DIRECTORY under projects/ (not files), to dir_list.txt. find can filter by type.

checks.fail: dir_list.txt must list every directory under projects/ including nested ones (type filter: d).

tasks.brief: Storage bills exploded. Find every file under projects/ LARGER THAN 100 kilobytes, to big_list.txt (find compares sizes with +/- prefixes).

checks.fail: big_list.txt must list only files over 100k (size test with a + prefix).

tasks.brief: The time bombs: files under projects/ that ANYONE can write (world-writable). Their paths to danger_list.txt (find tests permissions; -perm with a mode).

checks.fail: danger_list.txt must list the world-writable files (permission test for the world-write bit, e.g. -perm -002).

tasks.brief: Every EMPTY file under projects/ is a husk from the failed migration: their paths to empty_list.txt (find has an emptiness test).

checks.fail: empty_list.txt must list only the empty FILES under projects/ (combine the type filter with the empty test so empty directories stay out).

tasks.brief: Now act: find every *.swp under projects/ again and DELETE them in the same find command (find can execute actions; its delete action or an exec rm). The .swp files must be gone; everything else stays.

checks.fail: There are still *.swp files under projects/.
Non-target files were deleted too. The sweep was supposed to remove ONLY the .swp droppings.

tasks.brief: The compliance cover sheet: ONE number - how many total FILES (not directories) live under projects/ after your cleanup - to filecount.txt (find piped into the counter you mastered in Mission 10).

checks.fail: filecount.txt must contain the number of files under projects/ after the .swp cleanup (find type f piped into wc -l).
Config content changed during the sweep. Compliance sweeps observe and remove targets - they never edit.

tasks.brief: BONUS: which files under projects/ were modified in the last 24 hours? Their paths to recent_list.txt (find tests modification time in days with -mtime; 'less than one day ago' has a - prefix).

checks.fail: recent_list.txt must list the files modified within the last day (-mtime with a minus, type f).
